task.description: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (WF-02 Step 1b) hard gate on REQ-156's design at lib/letflow/design/req156-lua-memory-limit-impl.md. First review pass. Verify: (1) every one of REQ-156's 7 real acceptance_criteria (read docs/requirements.yaml directly) is mapped to a concrete design element; (2) NO literal Elixir code anywhere in the design -- grep for `fn `, `raise `, `case `, `cond `, `do:`, `->` and manually verify every hit is either a permitted @spec/@type signature or prose, including inside table cells; this exact check failed REQ-157's design twice this session; (3) CODE-DESIGNER's claim that Task.Supervisor.async_nolink/2,3 cannot carry a spawn_opt-equivalent option is independently verified against real Elixir source (if the Elixir/Erlang installation's source is available in this environment, e.g. under an asdf install path or via `elixir -e`, check task/supervisor.ex and task/supervised.ex directly; if source isn't available, verify the claim is at least internally consistent and doesn't contradict anything in Elixir's documented Task API); (4) the proposed alternative mechanism (raw :erlang.spawn_opt/2 + :monitor path bypassing Task.Supervisor for the memory-limited case) is a coherent, complete design that genuinely achieves the same unlink/monitor/kill semantics REQ-155 established for the Task.Supervisor path, not a hand-wave; (5) the :killed-reason ambiguity between a BEAM heap-kill and a caller-issued timeout-kill is resolved by a sound mechanism (read the design's proposed resolution and assess whether it's actually race-free); (6) the {:error, :memory_limit_exceeded} shape is genuinely distinguishable from REQ-154's and REQ-155's error shapes; (7) required moduledoc content (LUA-09 clause table: terminate MET, fail-gracefully NOT MET; :max_instructions rejection) is specified; (8) open questions are explicit, not silently resolved.
acceptance_criteria: All 7 REQ-156 acceptance criteria mapped to concrete design elements
Zero literal Elixir code anywhere in the design doc
The Task.Supervisor spawn_opt limitation claim independently verified or at minimum assessed for internal consistency
The alternative spawn_opt/monitor mechanism assessed as coherent and complete, not hand-waved
The :killed-reason race resolution assessed as sound

result.summary: Literal Elixir code found embedded in a table cell in lib/letflow/design/req156-lua-memory-limit-impl.md, §5, line 181. This is the exact failure mode that sank REQ-157's sibling design three times this session. All other checks passed but per WF-02 Step 1b, a single failed check is a total FAIL -- no partial credit.

checks.acceptance_criteria_mapping: PASS - all 7 REQ-156 ACs from docs/requirements.yaml mapped to concrete design elements in §8, each citing the specific section/table that satisfies it.
checks.no_literal_code: FAIL - line 181, §5 table (row for `max_heap_words` = nil): `Task.Supervisor.async_nolink(Letflow.Engine.Lua.TaskSupervisor, fn -> run_script(script_source, budget) end)`. This is a literal function-call expression with an anonymous-function literal (`fn -> ... end`), not a @spec/@type signature, and it is inside a table cell -- both markers explicitly called out as forbidden in this session's prior REQ-157 rework cycles.
checks.async_nolink_spawn_opt_claim: PASS, independently verified against installed source at /home/tvolodi/.asdf/installs/elixir/1.20.3-otp-29/lib/elixir/lib/task/supervisor.ex and task/supervised.ex (matches .tool-versions pin). Confirmed `@type async_opts :: [shutdown: :brutal_kill | timeout()]` (supervisor.ex line ~93) is the only key accepted for async/async_nolink options, and Task.Supervised.start_link/2,3 and start/3 (supervised.ex lines 9-18) call bare `spawn/4` and `spawn_link/3`/`spawn_link/4` with no options list -- no spawn_opt path exists in this call chain. Design's claim is accurate.
checks.alternative_mechanism_coherence: PASS - the :erlang.spawn_opt/2 with [:monitor, max_heap_size: ...] path (§2, §5) is a coherent, complete substitute: :monitor as a spawn_opt element atomically returns {pid, ref} (documented OTP 24+ behavior), giving the same unlinked+monitored relationship as async_nolink without a race window between spawn and monitor/1.
checks.killed_reason_race_resolution: PASS - §5.3's resolution is structural (ordering-based, not reason-inspection-based): the caller only issues its own kill after its bounded wait has already expired, so any :killed DOWN observed during the wait cannot originate from the caller. Sound and race-free as described.
checks.error_shape_distinguishability: PASS - §4.1 confirms three structurally distinct shapes: {:budget_exceeded, limit} (REQ-154), {:wallclock_timeout, ms} (REQ-155), bare :memory_limit_exceeded (REQ-156) -- no pattern-match ambiguity.
checks.moduledoc_content: PASS - §7 specifies all required content: LUA-09 clause table (terminate MET / fail-gracefully NOT MET), decision-0014 OQ-1 :max_instructions rejection, the async_nolink finding, the branching mechanism, and the observability divergence.
checks.open_questions_explicit: PASS - §10 lists 5 open questions (OQ-1..OQ-5), none silently resolved, each with a blocking/non-blocking disposition stated.

instructions_for_code_designer: Remove the literal Elixir expression at §5 line 181's table cell: `Task.Supervisor.async_nolink(Letflow.Engine.Lua.TaskSupervisor, fn -> run_script(script_source, budget) end)`.

Replace with prose describing the same fact without executable syntax, e.g.: 'Unchanged from REQ-155: the script body is submitted to Letflow.Engine.Lua.TaskSupervisor via async_nolink/2 exactly as REQ-155 §4.1-§4.3 already specify, byte-for-byte' -- name the function (async_nolink/2) and its arguments' roles in prose/table-cell text without writing out a callable expression or an fn/anonymous-function literal.

Re-grep the entire document for `fn `, `raise `, `case `, `cond `, `do:`, `->` after the edit and manually confirm every remaining hit is either inside a @spec/@type fence or is prose (e.g. the word 'case' used as an English noun, as at line 203, which is fine and was not flagged as a violation).

No other changes required -- all other checks (AC mapping, source-verified async_nolink claim, alternative mechanism, :killed race resolution, error-shape distinguishability, moduledoc content, open questions) passed and should not be altered.
